summary: Today’s pulse tracks Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile, Serbia votes as strongman Vučić faces grassroots challenge to 12-year rule – Europe live, and Ali G: Who Iz I? stooge says he was in on joke but didn’t tell Sacha Baron Cohen: ‘He’s not going to punk me. I’ll trick him’. Across BBC, Guardian, and NPR, the strongest repeated signals are serbia, storm, and england. In the background, Early reports suggest record high turnout in Serbia elections and More than 82,000 properties without power as Storm Boelo batters UK keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile
headlines.description: Machado had left the country just a month before the US government seized Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.

headlines.title: Serbia votes as strongman Vučić faces grassroots challenge to 12-year rule – Europe live
headlines.description: The Student List movement is taking on authoritarian leader following nearly two years of protests against government and institutional corruption What is at stake in Serbia’s election? Serbia’s former president and now prime ministerial candidate (again) Aleksandar Vučić rose to prominence in the 1990s as a radical nationalist, who supported the policies of Serbian expansion and ethnic cleansing led by Slobodan Milošević, who died of a heart attack in detention in The Hague during his trial on charges of genocide and crimes against humanity committed in Croatia, Bosnia and Kosovo. He served as Milošević’s information minister throughout the Kosovo conflict. His Serbian Progressive Party, or SNS, has been in government since 2012.

headlines.title: Ali G: Who Iz I? stooge says he was in on joke but didn’t tell Sacha Baron Cohen: ‘He’s not going to punk me. I’ll trick him’
headlines.description: Exclusive: Joshua Loudermilk says suspicions first raised during filming by gun shaped like wearable plastic bottom: ‘You’re gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that’ • This article contains spoilers for Ali G: Who Iz I? Joshua Loudermilk, one of two men apparently discredited by the new Ali G movie Ali G: Who Iz I?, has said that he was in on the joke, but that the film-makers didn’t realise this. Loudermilk, a 54-year-old aspiring actor from North Carolina, has told the Guardian he recognised star Sacha Baron Cohen early in the shoot but continued pretending to be a hard-right Maga sympathiser prepared to defend the US border at all costs.

headlines.title: Early reports suggest record high turnout in Serbia elections
headlines.description: Serbia is heading to the polls as a student movement attempts to oust longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vučić.

headlines.title: More than 82,000 properties without power as Storm Boelo batters UK
headlines.description: Met Office reports gusts of up to 84mph after weather warnings issued across Scotland, Northern Ireland and north of England More than 82,000 properties have been left without power as Storm Boelo continues to batter Scotland, Northern Ireland and the north of England. The adverse weather hitting northern parts of the UK on Saturday evening was the second named storm in as many days, after Storm Austen brought strong winds to south-west England on Friday.

headlines.title: Israelis have changed. Will they change their leadership?
headlines.description: Israel is holding a general election this week after years of war. For many Israelis, shaken by the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks and years of war, it is the most consequential in decades.

headlinePool.description: He will be observed to evaluate whether his "psychiatric health is compatible with pursuing his interrogation", authorities said.

headlinePool.title: Portuguese police with dogs and batons dismantle housing protest camps
headlinePool.description: More than 30 people arrested as officers clear at least 100 tents in central Lisbon and about 50 in Porto Police in Portugal have dismantled housing protest camps in Lisbon and Porto, baton-charging campaigners in the early hours of Sunday and arresting more than 30 people. The raids were the latest incident in days of clashes between police and campaigners who – inspired by similar camps in Spain – had sought to pitch tents in central squares to protest against the country’s deepening housing crisis.

headlinePool.title: Twelve injured, including six juveniles, in shooting near Florida university
headlinePool.description: Police say altercation at a homecoming party escalated into gunfire and they are working to identify ‘those responsible’ A shooting ⁠near a Florida university campus in Tallahassee has left 11 people ⁠with gunshot wounds ⁠and ​another person injured, authorities say. The shooting took place near the Florida Agricultural + Mechanical University’s campus ⁠on Perry Street on Saturday night, the university said, while police counted six adults and six ⁠juveniles among the injured.

headlinePool.title: What makes a good spine-tingler? Stephen Graham Jones says it's all in the ending
headlinePool.description: Horror writer Stephen Graham Jones says horror's current moment is powered by more than just fear.

headlinePool.title: Brazilians vote in presidential election runoff pitting leftist Lula against far-right Bolsonaro
headlinePool.description: Incumbent president lost in first round to senator and son of convicted ex-president Brazilians are going to the polls on Sunday in a highly unpredictable runoff in which the leftist president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva , is attempting an unprecedented comeback against the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro , who won the first-round vote. Bolsonaro’s surprise victory despite not leading most polls made him the favourite three weeks ago, but since then Lula’s campaign has gained ground, and the two go into the contest virtually tied.

headlinePool.title: Gabon says access to social media restored after eight-month ban
headlinePool.description: The authorities had justified the ban by saying online content was fuelling conflict, while the opposition had condemned it as an abuse of power.

headlinePool.title: Suspect in shooting death of teen on Missouri highway charged in second road incident
headlinePool.description: Man accused of shooting teen, who was driving to a party, has also been linked to shooting of a vehicle days earlier A man accused in the shooting death of a Missouri teen has been charged in a second shooting incident – both of which involve firing into cars on the highway. Alyssa Wilson, 17, was shot and killed as she drove down Interstate 170 in Overland, Missouri, on 14 October. The teen was on her way to a Halloween party at St Louis Zoo, called Boo at the Zoo, when a suspect fired a single shot into the back of Wilson’s Buick Encore.

headlinePool.title: Almost two-thirds of Australians bulk-billed for all GP care amid extra incentives for doctors
headlinePool.description: Exclusive: RACGP survey reflects Medicare investments, but experts caution quality of care and outcomes also matter And almost two-thirds (63%) of Australians are now bulk-billed for all their GP care, up from 56% in both 2024 and 2025, which the report says is “likely a reflection of the federal government’s recent investment in Medicare bulk billing incentives”.

headlinePool.title: All aboard the TrainTok trend: spotters and staff boost rail content online
headlinePool.description: Number of videos about British trains doubles in three months as creators find audiences interested in workings of railways They are not just gathered at the end of your local train station platform any more. Now they are on your social media platforms too. Trainspotters have played a part in more than doubling the number of videos about British trains on TikTok in the last three months. According to the platform, the rise in rail content is also down to more people seeking information on cheap tickets, facts about the London Underground and tales from train staff.
